import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Submitting the final declaration. I merged the five reports and my own checks into one report. My recommendation: **build it**, but with a tighter contract than "sub-bullets". **Recommended design** - **Shape:** plain bullets placed as the first children under each Event Task. No drawer and no header line. The motivating case stays one line: "And retainers!" directly under "Swings!". - **What gets dropped:** directive lines, video-call boilerplate (Teams, Zoom, Meet, Webex), separator lines, and lines that only repeat the 📹 or 📍 link. A Teams-only invite writes nothing, so its row looks exactly like today. - **Who owns the bullets:** they follow Google until you edit them, the same way the title, time, badges, `#offclock`, `[buffer::]` and `[root::]` already work. Once you edit, nest under, or delete them, they're yours for good. You get one notice only if Google's text changes after your edit. - **Safety:** description text is treated as inert data, and a test runs Bob's real parsers on hostile sample text to prove nothing is picked up as a task, drawer, log or date. - **Limits and scope:** at most 8 lines, the last one linking to the rest in Google Calendar. Event Tasks and Maybe→Yes upgrades only; rows synced before the feature get bullets on their day's next sync. JSON reports a line count, never the text. `gcal.description: off` turns it off. **Changes to your request (called out in the report):** limiting it to Event Tasks; filtering beyond directive lines; the "follows Google until edited" ownership; the line cap; filling in older rows; keeping descriptions out of JSON; and the off switch. The ownership change partly overrides the "child bullets: You, never touched" rule, so it needs a new decision record. The report includes a draft. **Where the researchers disagreed, and my call** - **Write once vs. follow Google (3 to 2): I chose follow Google.** Writing once is the same silent staleness behind the 2026-10-31 Halloween row, where the root stayed wrong after you edited the event in Google. Sync also only runs automatically once a day, when the daily note is created, so updates arrive when you re-sync yourself. That's when you'd expect them. This is the most debatable call. Phase 2 of the plan is write-once on its own, so stopping there gets you the simpler version. - **Plain bullets vs. a drawer:** plain bullets. A drawer like `AGENDA` would fill capture's drawer suggestions, and capturing into it would mix your notes into Google's block. Gem's argument that a drawer folds better is wrong: folding a task hides its children, not the task line. - **Strip boilerplate (cdx said keep it):** strip it, but only recognized vendor blocks, never matching phrases inside ordinary text. **New things I found while checking the code and vault** - Bold text like `**WORK LOG**` is read as a real Work Log, so a description's `Work log` would create a fake log under the meeting. - The journal needs care: each new row record replaces the previous one. A later title or root update that leaves out the description state would make the row look pre-feature, and its bullets would be inserted a second time. Making the field required in the code prevents this. - The current HTML cleanup keeps the text inside `
